content: 1. Dronabinol is metabolized by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administered with other drugs affecting this pathway. 2. Dronedarone increases lopinavir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Lopinavir increases duvelisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raises duvelisib AUC, increasing the risk of toxicities. 4. Duvelisib increases lopinavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with duvelisib raises the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing toxicity risks. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered, and signs of toxicity should be monitored. 5. Efavirenz decreases lopinavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Lopinavir increases elagolix levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be needed. 7. Lopinavir increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is recommended when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 8. Lopinavir increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir/ritonavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. No data are available to alter current dosing recommendations. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 85 mg PO once daily with lopinavir/ritonavir, except for 400/100 mg BID. 9. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Enfortumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate that releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage. MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase free MMAE exposure, raising the incidence or severity of toxicities. 10. Lopinavir increases escitalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity and serotonin syndrome risk. 11. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases lopinavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Lopinavir increases estradiol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and associated toxicities. 13. Lopinavir increases levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Lopinavir increases eszopiclone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The starting dose of eszopiclone should be reduced to 1 mg/day. 15. Lopinavir increases ethosuximide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 16. Lopinavir increases etoposide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Lopinavir and etrasimod may increase each other's effects via QTc interval prolongation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Transient decreases in heart rate and AV conduction delays may occur when initiating etrasimod. Due to the potential for additive effects on heart rate, etrasimod may increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes when co-administered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging agents. 18. Etravirine decreases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases etravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Lopinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Lopinavir and ezogabine may increase each other's toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. The QT interval should be monitored when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to increase the QT interval. 21. Lopinavir increases felodipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Fluconazole increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Fludrocortisone decreases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Lopinavir increases flunisolide inhaled levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Lopinavir increases flurazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternatives should be considered if available. Lowering the benzodiazepine dose may be required. 26. Lopinavir increases fluticasone furoate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. 27. Fluvoxamine increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Fosamprenavir increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Fosaprepitant increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases fosaprepitant levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Fosphenytoin decreases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Lopinavir increases fostamatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib's major active metabolite). Monitoring for toxicities that may require fostamatinib dose reduction is advised. 32. Lopinavir and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 33. Lopinavir increases gefitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. 34. Lopinavir and gemtuzumab both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Lopinavir and gepirone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 36. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glimepiride due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Lopinavir may increase or decrease glipizide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glyburide due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Grapefruit increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Griseofulvin decreases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Lopinavir increases guanfacine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 42. Lopinavir increases hydrocodone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 43. Hydrocortisone decreases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Idelalisib increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided. 45. Lopinavir decreases ifosfamide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. 46. Iloperidone increases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 47. Indacaterol inhaled and lopinavir may increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 48. Indinavir increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases indinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Lopinavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Isoniazid increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Lopinavir increases istradefylline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Istradefylline increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 52. Itraconazole increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The adult maximum itraconazole dose should be limited to 200 mg/day in patients receiving lopinavir/ritonavir. 53. Lopinavir increases ivacaftor levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines should be consulted for precise dosage modification. 54. Lopinavir decreases ketamine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Ketoconazole increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ketoconazole doses greater than 200 mg/day are not recommended when used concurrently with lopinavir/ritonavir. 56. Lopinavir increases lacosamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dose reduction of lacosamide should be considered when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
